review: The hymn is the rapture expectation: 1:1–2 is 1 Thess 4:16–17 with Rev 1:7 (בֶּעָנָן), 2:1–4 is Isa 9:5 with Ps 24:8, 2:5–8 is 1 Thess 4:17 with Rev 7:17, and 3:1–8 is Rev 22:20 with Isa 25:8 (מָחָה דִּמְעָה) and Phil 3:21.

The shape is 2/8/8: stanza 1 is a two-line acclamation and stanzas 2–3 are eight short lines each; the payload keeps stanza 1 at two lines, because the print sets the themes in a couplet before the hymn proper begins.

3:2 חֲתָנֵנוּ הֶחָבִיב — the Arabic عَرِيسَنَا الْحَبِيب is 'our beloved Bridegroom'; the Hebrew uses חָתָן, the bridegroom-word of Isa 62:5 and Matt 25:6, rather than the later רֵעַ or a circumlocution, so the bride-language of the hymn stays marital.

2:8 מוֹשִׁיעַ הַגְּוִיּוֹת — the Arabic مُخَلِّصَ الْأَجْسَاد is literally 'Saviour of the bodies'; the Hebrew keeps גְּוִיָּה, the poetic body-word of Job 19:26, because the line is about the resurrection of the body and not about deliverance in general.
